title: Honua npm registry search observations (v1)
description: Dated, reproducible observations of where this repository's published packages actually rank in npm registry search for the declared discovery terms (honua-io/honua-sdk-js#499, REQ-004). Each observation is immutable: re-observing a query ADDS a record with its own observedAt rather than rewriting an existing one, so an unflattering rank cannot be quietly edited away.

registry.description: How the observation was taken. Recorded so a reader can rerun the exact query rather than trusting the number.

endpoint.description: The npm registry search endpoint queried. Must be the registry itself: a rank read off a third-party mirror is not a primary observation.

resultsPerPage.description: Results per page on npmjs.com, used to convert a rank into the page a human sees. 'Page one' claims are meaningless without it.

scanDepth.description: How many ranked results were scanned before a package is reported as not found. A 'not found' claim is only as strong as this number.

trackedPackages.description: The packages this repository publishes and therefore looks for in every observation. A package absent from this list cannot be reported on the generated page.

observation.description: One measurement. It carries no interpretation: why a query is tracked, and whether it is a declared target, live in scripts/lib/npm-search-observations.mjs so a data file cannot restate its own purpose to suit its result.

query.description: The exact search text sent to the registry. Must be one of the queries declared in code.

expiresAt.description: When this observation stops standing for the current state of npm search. Rankings drift; an expired observation is reported as stale rather than silently reused.

totalResults.description: Total matches the registry reported for the query at observation time.

hits.description: One entry per tracked package, whether or not it was found. Omitting a package that did not rank is exactly the kind of selective reporting this format exists to prevent.

published.description: Whether the package existed on the registry when the observation was taken. An unpublished package cannot rank, so reporting it as merely 'not found' would overstate a discoverability problem that has not been tested yet.

rank.description: 1-based position in the registry's ranked results. Required when found, forbidden when not.

version.description: The version the registry returned for the ranked package.
